entities.summary: Abkhaz is a modern language with a complex history spanning centuries. It was first mentioned in the 5th century AD, during the Byzantine Empire, when it was used as a liturgical language in the Abkhazian Orthodox Church. The language gained prominence in the 13th century with the arrival of the Mongols, who conquered the region and adopted Abkhaz as their administrative language. Abkhaz was also used as a diplomatic language during the Golden Horde period, with the Abkhazian ambassador serving as a key figure in the relations between the Mongols and the Byzantine Empire. In the 19th century, Abkhaz was revived as a national language, with the establishment of the Abkhazian Language Society in 1905. Today, Abkhaz is an official language of Abkhazia, a breakaway region of Georgia, and is spoken by approximately 1 million people around the world. The language has had a significant impact on the intellectual and practical discourse of the region, influencing the development of various fields, including literature, art, and science.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Abkhaz language has had a significant impact on the intellectual and practical discourse of the region, influencing the development of various fields, including literature, art, and science. The language has also played a crucial role in the cultural identity of the Abkhaz people and has been recognized as an official language by the international community.
